meta.purpose: Per-state public-records access profiles for P0 FOIA sourcing (docs/plans/P0_foia_sourcing.md). Data, not logic: the FOIA-worthiness scorer reads jurisdiction_access from here; humans use it to pick where to file this week.
meta.authority: Reporters Committee (RCFP) Open Government Guide + police bodycam access map; MuckRock + Ballotpedia state guides. VERIFY each state against its RCFP page (rcfp url below) before filing — laws change and per-agency policy varies. broad general law != easy police video.
meta.coverage: 12 actionable states (tier-1 file-first, tier-2 caveated, avoid). Extend to all 50 as needed.

scoring.use: multiplier in foia_worth = EWU_shape_severity x records_likely_exist x jurisdiction_access x filing_window
scoring.note: Multipliers are PLACEHOLDERS — tune once real filing outcomes exist.

states.statute: Public Records Act, Fla. Stat. ch. 119
states.response_deadline_note: No fixed statutory deadline; must acknowledge/produce promptly within a reasonable time.
states.bodycam_rule: Public record. Exemptions: active criminal investigation; BWC taken inside a private residence, a health-care/mental-health facility, or a scene of a death/that shows the killing of a person.
states.audio_911_rule: 911 audio is a public record (releasable); the deceased's 911 death-call audio is exempt but a transcript is available.
states.fee_regime: Reasonable duplication cost; 'extensive use' special service charge allowed for large/complex requests.
states.notes: The archetypal sunshine state — broadest presumption of openness in the nation. Best first target.

states.response_deadline_note: 5 business days to respond/acknowledge (RCW 42.56.520); actual production can take longer on a reasonable schedule.
states.bodycam_rule: Disclosable but BWC is exempt under RCW 42.56.240(14) to the extent nondisclosure protects privacy; recordings inside a residence / of intimate scenes are presumed highly offensive. Non-privileged requesters may be charged redaction costs.
states.audio_911_rule: 911/CAD generally public; standard PRA privacy redactions apply.
states.fee_regime: Copying/customized-service fees; requester may bear BWC redaction cost (RCW 42.56.240(14)) unless a directly-involved party.
states.notes: Very strong PRA, narrow exemptions; some agencies self-publish BWC (Seattle PD YouTube). Main friction = redaction cost + privacy presumptions.

states.statute: California Public Records Act (Gov. Code sec. 7920 et seq.) + SB 1421 (2019) + SB 16 (2021) + AB 748
states.response_deadline_note: 10 days to determine whether records are disclosable (+14 in unusual circumstances). Critical-incident video: released at earliest possible time, no later than 45 days (may be withheld up to 45 days during active investigation).
states.bodycam_rule: Critical-incident BWC (officer-involved shooting, great-bodily-injury use of force) released within 45 days (AB 748 / SB 16). Misconduct records unsealed by SB 1421/SB 16: sexual assault, significant/unreasonable use of force, dishonesty, unlawful arrest/search, discrimination, failure to intervene.
states.fee_regime: Direct cost of duplication; redaction time generally not chargeable to requester.
states.notes: Already the project backbone (SDPD, SFDPA). Strong SPECIFICALLY for critical-incident + misconduct records; routine non-incident BWC is more discretionary.

states.response_deadline_note: No fixed deadline; must produce within a reasonable period of time.
states.bodycam_rule: BWC is a public record; specific restricted portions exempt (e.g. inside a residence, victims of certain crimes, death images). Courts lean toward disclosure.
states.notes: Open records tradition; the 'no deadline' language means follow-up pressure matters.

states.statute: Open Records Act, O.C.G.A. sec. 50-18-70 et seq.
states.response_deadline_note: 3 business days to produce or state a timeline + cost estimate.
states.bodycam_rule: BWC generally accessible; pending-investigation and privacy redactions apply.
states.fee_regime: Copying + reasonable search/retrieval after first 15 min.
states.notes: Fast statutory deadline is a plus. (Historic residency limit no longer enforced — open to any person.)

states.statute: Public Records Law, A.R.S. sec. 39-121 et seq.
states.bodycam_rule: Public record subject to the best-interests-of-the-state / privacy balancing test; BWC releasable with redactions.
states.fee_regime: Copying cost; commercial-purpose requests pay more.
states.notes: Strong presumption of openness; the balancing test adds discretion.

states.statute: Public Records Law, Wis. Stat. sec. 19.31-19.39
states.response_deadline_note: 'As soon as practicable and without delay' — no fixed deadline.
states.bodycam_rule: BWC subject to a common-law/statutory balancing test; releasable, with a specific carve-out balancing for recordings in residences/of victims.
states.fee_regime: Location + copying; no charge under $50 for some categories.
states.notes: Strong openness tradition; discretion via balancing test.

states.statute: CORA (C.R.S. sec. 24-72-200.1) for records + CCJRA (sec. 24-72-301) for criminal-justice records
states.response_deadline_note: 3 working days, extendable to 7 for extenuating circumstances (CORA).
states.bodycam_rule: 2021 law requires release of BWC of an alleged misconduct incident within 21 days; but general criminal-justice records under CCJRA are CUSTODIAN-DISCRETIONARY.
states.audio_911_rule: Audio recordings disclosure required in relevant contexts; courts have ordered BWC release.
states.fee_regime: Research/retrieval fee after first hour; per-page copying.
states.notes: Split regime: strong for misconduct BWC (21-day rule) but discretionary for general criminal-justice records. Frame requests around the misconduct hook.

states.statute: Public Information Act, Tex. Gov. Code ch. 552
states.response_deadline_note: Produce promptly; to withhold, must ask the AG for a ruling within 10 business days.
states.bodycam_rule: BWC releasable, but the 'dead-suspect loophole' (sec. 552.108) lets agencies withhold records of cases that did NOT end in conviction/deferred adjudication — a major gap for OIS/in-custody-death cases.
states.fee_regime: Charges set by Attorney General cost rules.
states.notes: The dead-suspect loophole directly hits our best case types (fatal OIS). Expect denials on non-conviction cases; still worth trying + appealing.

states.statute: Right-to-Know Law (RTKL), 65 P.S. sec. 67.101 + Act 22 of 2017 for audio/video
states.response_deadline_note: RTKL: 5 business days (extendable 30). BUT bodycam/dashcam is REMOVED from the RTKL by Act 22.
states.bodycam_rule: Act 22 routes BWC requests OUTSIDE the RTKL: written request within 60 DAYS of the recording, by certified mail, agency has 30 days to deny, and denials are appealed to COURT (not the Office of Open Records) with a filing fee.
states.fee_regime: RTKL copying fees; Act 22 process may add cost.
states.notes: AVOID for bodycam — Act 22's 60-day window + certified-mail + court-appeal process is denial-prone and slow.

states.statute: Virginia FOIA, Va. Code sec. 2.2-3700 et seq.
states.bodycam_rule: Criminal investigative files are DISCRETIONARY to release (sec. 2.2-3706); BWC often withheld as part of a criminal file.
states.notes: AVOID: RESIDENTS/VA-media only (upheld by SCOTUS) AND law-enforcement records are discretionary. Would need a VA-resident/media requester.

states.statute: Freedom of Information Law (FOIL), N.Y. Pub. Off. Law sec. 84-90
states.response_deadline_note: 5 business days to acknowledge; actual production frequently takes months.
states.bodycam_rule: BWC accessible in principle since the 2020 repeal of Civil Rights Law 50-a, but agencies (esp. NYPD) are slow and heavily redact; long backlogs.
states.audio_911_rule: 911 generally obtainable via FOIL but slow.
states.notes: AVOID for speed: law is fine post-50a but response latency is severe. Not a fast funnel.
